answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can treat reputation like an orchard: each identity starts as a single sapling and only bears fruit after seasons of verified work, so planting a thousand fake trees costs a thousand seasons. Newcomers enter through one narrow inlet - a small bonded task with peer review - instead of an open gate, and trust flows like water past a willow: slow, visible, and hard to fake in bulk. Mass fakery then costs more than it earns.
